reasons: No tests are visible in the packet.
Empty results and loading states are handled.
Capacity totals mix units, which the page itself labels as mixed basis.

terms.meaning: The set of projects that are planned or under way, not yet finished.
A key date in a project's life, such as final investment decision or commercial operation date.
The source quote and link that back up a value shown on the page.
Splitting a long list into pages so only part of it loads at once.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the pipeline page
sections.what: Brings in the display helpers, data loading tools, table pieces, date slider, milestone picker, icons, routing, and evidence tools.
sections.why: Needed to draw the table and load the projects it shows.

sections.name: evField
sections.title: Building evidence for a value
sections.what: Takes a project and a field name and packages the value with its first source link, publisher, quote, and location. If there is no evidence, the fields are left empty rather than made up.
sections.why: Lets each table cell open its source without inventing a citation.
sections.watch_out: Only the first evidence entry is used, so a field with several sources shows just one.

sections.name: SortKey
sections.title: Sortable column names
sections.what: Lists the field names the table can sort by.
sections.why: Keeps sort choices to a known list that the server understands.
sections.watch_out: Each name must match what the server accepts for sorting.

sections.name: MISSING_LABELS
sections.title: Short labels for missing fields
sections.what: Maps field names to short labels used on the missing-data chips, such as Budget or EPC.
sections.why: Keeps the missing-data chips short so they fit in the table.
sections.watch_out: A field missing from this list shows its raw name instead.

sections.name: COLUMNS
sections.title: Table column definitions
sections.what: Defines the table headers in order, with a label, a sort key, and a width for each column. The COD column has no sort key.
sections.why: Keeps the header row and the body rows in step.
sections.watch_out: The COD column uses an empty key cast to any type, so it is not sortable and the cast hides this from the type checker.

sections.name: formatNa
sections.title: Empty value display
sections.what: Shows a grey N/A tag when a value is missing, and otherwise returns the value unchanged.
sections.why: Makes missing data visible and consistent.

sections.name: formatBudget
sections.title: Budget display
sections.what: Shows a budget as a formatted amount, or an N/A tag when there is no budget.
sections.why: Keeps budget formatting in one place.

sections.name: formatBudgetCell
sections.title: Budget cell display
sections.what: Chooses how to show the planned budget. It prefers a low to high range, then a single amount, then the original text from the report with a document icon, and finally N/A.
sections.why: Projects store budgets in different forms, and the cell shows the most precise one available.
sections.watch_out: The fallback text is cut short, so long budget notes are only visible on hover.

sections.name: statusVariant
sections.title: Status colour choice
sections.what: Maps a project status to a badge style, such as red for critical risk or over budget and outline for completed.
sections.why: Lets users spot trouble statuses at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Any status not listed falls back to the default style.

sections.name: computeDateBounds
sections.title: Date slider limits
sections.what: Works out the earliest and latest dates for the slider from the chosen milestone field. If that field is empty for all projects, it uses fid, construction start, and commercial operation dates instead. The earliest date is at least the year 2000, and the latest is two years after the last date found.
sections.why: Makes the slider match the real dates in the data so the range starts and ends sensibly.
sections.watch_out: The default range is 2020 to 2040 when no dates exist, so projects outside that span can be hidden.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 1)
sections.title: Page state and citation handling
sections.what: Holds the chosen milestone, sort, date range, slider state, and page. It also sets up the full citation drawer and a helper that opens it for a given field. It loads the bounds set and resets the range when the milestone or first load changes.
sections.why: Keeps all user choices in one place so the table and slider stay in step.
sections.watch_out: The range is only set when there is no range yet, so a change in the data can leave an old range in place.

sections.name: Pipeline: if
sections.title: Request settings, sorting, and capacity total
sections.what: Builds the settings sent with each table request, adding the date range only when the slider is in use and adding the sub-industry when one is chosen. It then loads the page of projects, counts results and pages, and handles sort clicks, slider changes, and the total reported capacity.
sections.why: Sends only the filters the user has set, and keeps the sort toggling and paging consistent.
sections.watch_out: The capacity total is summed over the bounds set of up to 500 projects, not the full set, so it can differ from the table count.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 3)
sections.title: Heading, filters, and date slider
sections.what: Shows the page title, the record count, the current page, the segment chip, and the total capacity. It also shows the milestone picker, the date slider, and a clear button that appears when the slider is in use.
sections.why: Lets the user see the result size and change the filters that drive the table.
sections.watch_out: Clearing the filter resets the range to the full date span, which may not match the earlier view.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 4)
sections.title: Table body and empty states
sections.what: Shows a spinner while loading, a message when no projects match, or the table with a clickable row for each project. Each cell shows its value with a source popover.
sections.why: Gives clear feedback in every state and lets the user open any project.
sections.watch_out: Row navigation uses the industry slug, so the wrong slug sends the user to the wrong project list.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 5)
sections.title: Table cells for market and cost fields
sections.what: Shows cells for likelihood, confidence, planned and actual budget, delay, EPC contractor, and vendor. Each cell has its own source popover and the missing-data formatting.
sections.why: Keeps each value traceable to its source.
sections.watch_out: Some cells use a different fallback for missing values, so empty states may look different across columns.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 6)
sections.title: Table cells for dates and missing data
sections.what: Shows the commercial operation date, with the original date struck through when an updated date exists. It also shows chips for each missing field, or a Complete tag when none are missing.
sections.why: Shows changes to dates and the completeness of each record.
sections.watch_out: The strike-through only appears when an updated date exists, so a changed date with no updated value would look unchanged.

sections.name: Pipeline (part 7)
sections.title: Paging controls
sections.what: Shows first, previous, next, and last buttons, plus up to seven numbered page buttons that stay around the current page. The controls only appear when there is more than one page.
sections.why: Lets users move through long lists without loading everything at once.
sections.watch_out: Buttons are disabled at the ends, so the page number must stay within the valid range.

summary: This is the Pipeline page, a sortable and paged table of projects that are in the pipeline, with a date-range slider and a count of reported capacity.
purpose: Lets a user scan pipeline projects, sort them, filter them by a milestone date range, and open any project.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The table is designed to show evidence next to each value and to show missing data clearly.
how: The page first loads a larger set of pipeline projects to find the date limits. It then loads one page of projects with the chosen sort, date range, and sub-industry. The table shows each value with its evidence and marks missing fields. Users can change the milestone type, drag the date slider, click headers to sort, and move between pages.
inputs: The current industry from the industry context, the optional sub-industry from the segment state, and the user's choices for milestone, sort, date range, and page.
outputs: A rendered table with counts, capacity totals, paging controls, and a citation drawer when evidence is opened.
risks: The date limits are based on only the first 500 projects, so the range may miss later records. The total capacity line mixes units.
debug: If the table is empty, check the filters and the bounds query. If a value is missing, check the evidence map on the project record. If sorting does not change, check the sort key names against the server.
